reference_sql:
SELECT c.parent_category, c.category_name, COUNT(*) AS n_products,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY c.parent_category ORDER BY COUNT(*) DESC) AS size_rank
FROM products p
JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
GROUP BY c.parent_category, c.category_name
alternatives:
WITH category_size AS (  -- one row per category with products
  SELECT c.parent_category, c.category_name, COUNT(*) AS n_products
  FROM products p
  JOIN categories c ON c.category_id = p.category_id
  GROUP BY c.parent_category, c.category_name
)
SELECT cs.parent_category, cs.category_name, cs.n_products,
       1 + (SELECT COUNT(DISTINCT cs2.n_products) FROM category_size cs2
            WHERE cs2.parent_category = cs.parent_category AND cs2.n_products > cs.n_products) AS size_rank
FROM category_size cs

other_way.tradeoff: Counting the different larger sizes in a subquery gives the same place without a window, but it is harder to read.

solver.query:
WITH n AS (
  SELECT c.parent_category, c.category_name, COUNT(p.product_id) AS n_products
  FROM categories c
  LEFT JOIN products p ON p.category_id = c.category_id
  GROUP BY c.category_id, c.parent_category, c.category_name
)
SELECT parent_category, category_name, n_products,
       DENSE_RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY parent_category ORDER BY n_products DESC) AS size_rank
FROM n
